title: Saint Vincent
capsule: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a Caribbean island state comprising the main island of Saint Vincent and a chain of smaller Grenadine islands, achieving associated statehood with the United Kingdom in 1969 and full independence on 27 October 1979. The economy has historically depended on banana cultivation, tourism, and remittances, with vulnerability to hurricanes — most severely Hurricane Ivan (2004) and the La Soufrière eruptions of 2021 — repeatedly straining the state. Ralph Gonsalves has served as Prime Minister since 2001 under the Unity Labour Party, making him one of the longest-serving heads of government in the Caribbean. The country maintains membership in CARICOM, the Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States, and the Commonwealth.
